definitions.gloss: dumplings over flowers; substance over style
definitions.explanation: Practical benefits or material things are preferred over aesthetic pleasures or superficial beauty. Prioritizing what is useful or satisfying over what is merely beautiful.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{花|はな}より{団子|だんご}で、⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{弁当|べんとう}→弁当：01014_bentou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{楽|たの}しみにしていた→楽しみにする：26825_tanoshiminisuru⟧。
examples.english: She's the practical type—she was more excited about the bento than the cherry blossoms.

examples.japanese: {花|はな}より{団子|だんご}⟦という→という：09577_toiu⟧⟦タイプ→たいぷ：01534_taipu⟧な⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧、⟦デザイン→でざいん：03860_dezain⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{機能|きのう}→機能：13165_kinou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{重視|じゅうし}する→重視：03341_juushi⟧。
examples.english: Being the practical type, I prioritize function over design.

examples.japanese: ⟦{美術館|びじゅつかん}→美術館：01717_bijutsukan⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{食|た}べ{放題|ほうだい}→食べ放題：08291_tabehoudai⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}きたい→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦なんて→なんて：06918_nante⟧、{花|はな}より{団子|だんご}⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧⟦ね→ね：09474_ne⟧。
examples.english: Wanting to go to an all-you-can-eat place rather than an art museum—how practical of you!

notes:
ORIGIN: This proverb originates from the Japanese custom of ⟦{花見|はなみ}→花見：01700_hanami⟧ (cherry blossom viewing), where people gather to appreciate the beauty of cherry blossoms. The proverb humorously observes that many people are more interested in the food and drink (⟦{団子|だんご}→団子：04959_dango⟧, dumplings, representing refreshments) than in the flowers themselves.

USAGE: Used to describe someone who values practical or material benefits over aesthetic or cultural experiences. Can be used self-deprecatingly or to tease others. Often used with ～というタイプ or as a standalone comment.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{実|じつ}→実：28344_jitsu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{取|と}る→取る：00565_toru⟧ (to take the substance)
- ⟦{名|な}→名：03496_na⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧⟦{実|じつ}→実：28344_jitsu⟧ (substance over reputation)

ENGLISH EQUIVALENT: "Substance over style" or "bread is better than the songs of birds"

CULTURAL NOTE: The proverb is not necessarily negative—it can simply describe a practical, down-to-earth personality. It appears in the title of a popular manga/drama series, bringing renewed attention to the phrase.
